name: Sergei
desc: My name is Sergei, I am a DevOps Engineer and you are on my webpage.

resume.text: I am a DevOps engineer with 7+ years of experience (4+ years in DevOps & Cloud Infrastructure + 3+ years as a Backend developer). Currently focused on professional growth in cloud-native technologies, CI/CD automation, and infrastructure as code.

I have extensive hands-on experience in setting up end-to-end Pipelines using TeamCity and Jenkins; writing scripts to publish artifacts to Nexus and DockerHub; building and orchestrating containers with Docker and Docker-compose; managing Kubernetes clusters; provisioning infrastructure with Terraform across Google Cloud Platform, Amazon Web Services, and Yandex Cloud; configuration management with Ansible; and monitoring with Zabbix, ELK Stack (Fluentd & ElasticSearch & Kibana), and Prometheus stack (Prometheus & Node-Exporter & Alertmanager & Grafana).

I continuously improve my skills by exploring new technologies, earning certifications, and applying best practices in real-world projects. My goal is to design and maintain robust, scalable, and secure infrastructure that empowers development teams to ship faster and with confidence.

text.text: «The price of greatness is responsibility.» Winston Churchill.

This phrase can sound pretentious, but I completely agree with it, because I consider that the main professional quality of a man is responsibility. Speaking about myself, I can say with no hesitation that responsibility - is one of my strongest qualities. No doubt that I am not the best developer in the world, for sure I don't know each and every aspect of DevOps technologies and etc. But I have a very high level of responsibility. If I got down to work, the work will be done, while studying the technology, so that next time there will be no difficulties if they nevertheless arise.
Generally speaking, I can find out within myself these professional qualities:

selfedu.text: Self-education has been a big part of my life for many years. Generally speaking, a person can feel “okay” just by learning and applying one narrow stack of technologies. But I always feel the need to “look around” for exciting new technological opportunities. That is why I try to learn new technologies that I can use in my future work.

For self-education, I regularly use the documentation of a particular technology, deploy VMs for “experiments”, and of course I try to communicate with competent people who can suggest what should be emphasized.
